2609.04855.title: CC-Mediation: Evaluating Large Language Models for Cross-Cultural Conflict Mediation
2609.04855.paper_summary: Cross-cultural mediation by large language models (LLMs) requires deciding both when to intervene and how to respond in culturally grounded conflicts. Progress on this problem has been limited by the lack of (1) mediation datasets with measurable downstream effects and (2) principled metrics for evaluating intercultural stance change. To address these gaps, we introduce CC-Mediation, a cross-cultural mediation benchmark of $1{,}661$ ten-turn dialogues grounded in the Developmental Model of Intercultural Sensitivity (DMIS), containing culturally grounded conflicts, mediation interventions, and post-intervention trajectories. We further propose two DMIS-based evaluation metrics: Trajectory AUC, which measures the persistence of intercultural improvement over time, and a signed Wasserstein-1 distance, which measures the magnitude and direction of shifts in intercultural stance. Both metrics show strong agreement with human judgment of DMIS-grounded stance shift. Using CC-Mediation, we find that current LLMs have limitations on both axes: intervention timing (when) failure stems from a positional prior that ignores dialogue content, while mediation strategy (how) failure arises from a late-layer elicitation collapse rather than a knowledge deficit.
2609.04855.paper_summary_zh: 跨文化的媒介由大型語言模型（LLMs）進行，需要決定何時介入以及如何在文化根植的衝突中作出回應。對於這個問題的進展受到以下兩個因素的限制：（1）缺乏具有可測量下游效果的媒介數據集，以及（2）缺乏評估跨文化立場變化的原則性指標。為了解決這些空白，我們介紹了CC-Mediation，一個基於跨文化媒介的基準，包含$1{,}661$個基於發展模型的跨文化敏感性（DMIS）的十輪對話，涵蓋文化根植的衝突、媒介介入和介入後的軌跡。我們進一步提出了兩個基於DMIS的評估指標：軌跡AUC，測量跨文化改善隨時間的持續性，以及簽名Wasserstein-1距離，測量跨文化立場變化的幅度和方向。這兩個指標與人類對DMIS根植的立場變化的判斷顯示出強烈的一致性。使用CC-Mediation，我們發現當前的LLMs在這兩個方面都有局限性：介入時機（何時）的失敗源於一種忽略對話內容的立場先驗，而媒介策略（如何）的失敗則源於晚層引導崩潰，而非知識不足。
